answer.reason: The clause permits ('may') appointing team members from inside or outside the company, and the item restates this as optional.
The item keeps both the flexibility to set frequency by company requirements and the mandatory minimum of at least once a year.
The clause mandates that the frequency be stated in the procedure, which the item restates exactly.
The clause mandates a report at the completion of a self-inspection, matching the item.
The item lists all three mandatory report contents: results, evaluation and conclusions, and recommended corrective actions.
The clause mandates an effective follow-up programme; the reference to self-inspection outcomes is the clause's own context.
The clause mandates management evaluation of the report and corrective actions as necessary, which the item restates with equivalent meaning.
The clause says it 'may be useful' to supplement with a quality audit, matching the optional item.
The clause permits extending quality audits to suppliers and contractors, matching the optional item.
The item restates the mandatory QC responsibility, shared with other departments, for approving suppliers of materials meeting specifications.
The clause mandates evaluation before approval and inclusion in the approved suppliers' list or specifications, as the item states.
The item restates the mandatory evaluation factors: supplier history and nature of the materials.
The item keeps the condition 'if an audit is required' and the mandatory purpose of determining GMP conformance ability.
The item restates the recommended regular internal audits on an approved schedule to verify API GMP compliance.
The item restates the recommendation to document findings and corrective actions and bring them to responsible management.
The item restates the recommendation to complete agreed corrective actions in a timely and effective manner.
